chunks: Hamza b. Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Ja'far b. Muhammad b. Zayd b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim informed us, from his father, from Ali b. Ma'bad, from al-Husayn b. Khalid, from Abu'l Hasan Ali b. Musa al-Rida, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) said:

Whoever would like to board the Ark of Salvation, grapple onto the Firm Handle, and hold onto the firm Rope of Allah, should align with Ali after me, oppose his enemy, and accept the Imams of Guidance from his descendants; for surely, they are my vicegerents, my deputies, and the Proofs of Allah over His creation after me. They are the Masters of my Nation and the ones who will lead the pious to Paradise. Their party is my party, and my party is the Party of Allah, and their enemies' party is the Party of Satan.

key_terms.العروة الوثقي: The Firm Handle — from Quran 2:256, symbolizing the unbreakable bond with God
key_terms.حبل الله المتين: The firm Rope of Allah — from Quran 3:103, symbolizing divine guidance
key_terms.حجج الله: Proofs of Allah — a theological title for the Imams as divine representatives
key_terms.خلفائي وأوصيائي: My vicegerents and my deputies — designating the Imams as successors
key_terms.سفينة النجاة: Ark of Salvation — metaphor for the path to salvation, echoing the Ark of Noah

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about following Imam Ali and the Imams from his descendants?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition narrated through Imam al-Rida (AS) and the chain of Imams back to the Prophet (SAWW), the Prophet Muhammad emphatically declares the necessity of following Imam Ali and the Imams from his lineage. He uses three powerful Quranic metaphors — the Ark of Salvation (echoing Noah's Ark), the Firm Handle (al-Urwa al-Wuthqa from 2:256), and the Rope of Allah (Habl Allah from 3:103) — to describe the role of the Imams as the only path to salvation. The audience was the Muslim community, and the terms would have been immediately recognized as Quranic references, lending divine authority to the designation.
